label: API contract pin and safety invariants

map.subsystem: API contract pin and safety invariants (contract/ pin, ContractSmokeTest, SafetyConstantDriftGuardTest, ADRs 0001-0003, safety-constants SoT, SPDX header policy, AI-attribution enforcement)

capabilities.name: Vendored OpenAPI pin (contract/openapi.json)
capabilities.behavior: A byte-for-byte vendored copy of the backend monorepo's apps/api/contract/openapi.json. 748,299 bytes. `openapi: "3.1.0"`. Top-level keys are exactly `components`, `info`, `openapi`, `paths` — there is NO `servers` block and no top-level `security` block, so the pin carries no base URL and no auth scheme (base URL is user-set at runtime via BaseUrlInterceptor). `info` = {title: "GlycemicGPT API", version: "0.1.0", description: "AI-powered diabetes management API", x-contract-version: "1"} — note x-contract-version is a JSON *string*, read with getString. 164 paths, 274 component schemas. Never hand-edited: refresh means copying the whole file over. The pin is consumed only by tests; no runtime code reads it, and it is explicitly out of scope for SPDX stamping.
edge_cases: No `servers` key — the port cannot derive an endpoint host from the pin.
x-contract-version is a string, not an int, in the JSON.
Excluded from SPDX header stamping by policy.

capabilities.name: CONTRACT_VERSION file and version-agreement check
capabilities.behavior: contract/CONTRACT_VERSION is a 2-byte file containing `1` + newline. It must equal `info.x-contract-version` inside the pinned spec. Test `vendored CONTRACT_VERSION matches the pinned spec x-contract-version` reads the file via ContractFixtures.readRepoFile("contract/CONTRACT_VERSION").trim(), reads the spec string, and assertEquals(specVersion, fileVersion) — a string comparison, not numeric. Failure message tells the developer to "refresh the pin and its version together". Per ADR 0001, the semantic type is a monotonically increasing integer starting at 1, compared numerically at runtime once the compat signal ships; an unparseable value must be treated as absent, never as compatible. Refresh procedure: copy openapi.json, set CONTRACT_VERSION from the new spec, run ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest.
edge_cases: Test compares as strings; ADR mandates numeric semantics at runtime.
Both files must be updated in the same PR.

capabilities.name: ContractFixtures repo-root resolution helper
capabilities.behavior: object com.glycemicgpt.mobile.contract.ContractFixtures. `PINNED_SPEC_PATH = "contract/openapi.json"`. `repoRoot()` starts at File(System.getProperty("user.dir")).absoluteFile (the Gradle module project dir for unit tests) and walks up parentFile until it finds a directory containing a file named `settings.gradle.kts`; if it reaches null it calls error(...) with the starting dir. `readRepoFile(relativePath)` resolves against repoRoot(), `check(file.isFile)` with a message instructing the developer to update the guard and docs/contract/safety-constants.md if the file moved, then readText(). `pinnedSpec()` = JSONObject(readRepoFile(PINNED_SPEC_PATH)) — reparsed on every call, no caching. Both contract guards depend on this: they read repo files from disk, not from the test classpath.
edge_cases: Repo-root marker is settings.gradle.kts — moving/renaming it breaks both guards.
pinnedSpec() re-parses 748 KB of JSON per call (called many times per test run).

capabilities.name: ContractSmokeTest harness (real Retrofit + real Moshi)
capabilities.behavior: JUnit4 class in package com.glycemicgpt.mobile.data.remote. @Before: starts an okhttp3 MockWebServer, builds Retrofit with baseUrl = server.url("/") and MoshiConverterFactory.create(moshi), creates the REAL GlycemicGptApi interface. `moshi = Moshi.Builder().add(InstantAdapter()).build()` — deliberately byte-identical to NetworkModule.provideMoshi() so the test exercises the app's actual deserialization config (no bespoke adapters, no KotlinJsonAdapterFactory; DTOs use codegen @JsonClass(generateAdapter=true)). @After: server.shutdown(). `enqueue(body)` queues MockResponse().setBody(body) (HTTP 200, no headers). InstantAdapter: @ToJson uses DateTimeFormatter.ISO_INSTANT, @FromJson uses Instant.parse(value) — a non-ISO string throws DateTimeParseException, not JsonDataException.
edge_cases: Moshi config drift between NetworkModule and the test would silently weaken the guard; they must be kept identical by hand.
Instant parse failures surface as DateTimeParseException, which assertIncompatible would NOT accept (it requires a JsonDataException in the cause chain).

capabilities.name: Golden round-trip assertions (4 payloads)
capabilities.behavior: Hand-authored payloads written to match the pinned spec (NOT generated from it), deserialized through the real DTOs. (1) health: `{"status":"ok"}` → HealthResponse.status == "ok". (2) login: access_token/refresh_token/token_type/expires_in=3600/user{id,email,role} → LoginResponse.accessToken=="a", refreshToken=="r", expiresIn==3600, user.id=="u1". (3) alert thresholds: urgent_low=55.0, low_warning=70.0, high_warning=180.0, urgent_high=250.0 → Float comparisons with delta 0.0f; iob_warning absent → assertNull(iobWarning). (4) safety limits: min_glucose_mgdl=20, max_glucose_mgdl=500, max_basal_rate_milliunits=3000, max_bolus_dose_milliunits=25000, updated_at="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" → minGlucoseMgDl==20, maxGlucoseMgDl==500. These gate client-side DTO regressions; they do NOT by themselves detect backend drift.
edge_cases: Payloads are hand-written, so they can drift from the real spec without failing — only the endpoint-presence and field-presence tests couple to the pin.
The 55/70/180/250 threshold values are fixture values, not app defaults.

capabilities.name: Additive-drift tolerance assertions
capabilities.behavior: Two tests pin the client half of the tolerant-reader posture. (1) `unknown extra fields are ignored`: alert-thresholds payload plus `iob_warning:4.5`, `future_field:"ignored"`, `nested_future:{"a":1}` — parses fine; urgentLow==55.0f and iobWarning==4.5f. Moshi's generated adapters skip unknown keys by default, including unknown nested objects. (2) `optional field absent is tolerated (older backend)`: `{"glucose_unit":"mmol"}` → GlucoseUnitResponse.glucoseUnit=="mmol", glucoseUnitSource==null (the DTO declares `@Json(name="glucose_unit_source") val glucoseUnitSource: String? = null`). Together these encode: a newer backend adding fields, and an older backend predating an optional field, both stay readable. Kotlin default values on DTO constructor params are what make absent-optional tolerated.
edge_cases: A Swift Codable port defaults to throwing on missing keys — nullable-with-default semantics must be reproduced explicitly per field.

capabilities.name: Incompatible-drift assertions and assertIncompatible
capabilities.behavior: Three tests prove a consumed-field break fails loudly. (1) `access_token` renamed to `accessToken` in the login payload. (2) nested `user` object missing its required `id`. (3) `min_glucose_mgdl` sent as the string "twenty" instead of Int. Helper `assertIncompatible(block)` runs the suspend call under runBlocking, catches Throwable, asserts non-null ("Expected incompatible payload to fail parsing, but it parsed"), then walks the cause chain via generateSequence(thrown){it.cause} and asserts at least one link `is JsonDataException`. So the contract is specifically: Moshi must raise JsonDataException (missing required property / type mismatch) — any other failure type fails the test. Type coercion is NOT tolerated: a JSON string where an Int is declared is treated as incompatible.
edge_cases: Only JsonDataException counts; JsonEncodingException or DateTimeParseException would fail the assertion.
Nullable/defaulted consumed fields do NOT fail here — that is the documented blind spot.

capabilities.name: Endpoint-presence coupling to the pinned spec
capabilities.behavior: Test `every endpoint the app calls exists in the pinned spec`. Builds `specOps: Map<normalizedPath, Set<lowercased HTTP methods>>` from spec.paths. Reflects over `GlycemicGptApi::class.java.declaredMethods`, maps each through `retrofitOp` which checks, in order, @GET, @POST, @PUT, @DELETE, @PATCH and returns (lowercased verb, annotation value) or null. Results are `.distinct()`, then filtered to those where the normalized path is absent from specOps or the verb is not in that path's method set. `normalizePath` = `path.replace(Regex("\\{[^}]+}"), "{}")`, so Retrofit's `{deviceToken}` matches the spec's `{device_token}`. Asserts the missing list is empty with a message naming contract/openapi.json. Verified today: all 34 declared operations resolve; missing list is empty.
edge_cases: Path-parameter NAMES are erased by normalization — a backend renaming a path param is not caught.
Only checks presence of path+verb; request/response shapes for non-covered endpoints are unchecked.
Relies on Java reflection over a Kotlin interface; a Swift port needs an explicit endpoint table instead.

capabilities.name: Field-presence coupling for safety-critical responses
capabilities.behavior: Test `pinned spec still declares the safety-critical fields the app reads` couples directly to the pin (unlike the hand-written round-trips). assertConsumedFieldsPresent(path, method, fields) resolves the 200 → content["application/json"] → schema, follows a top-level `$ref` into components.schemas, and asserts every listed field is in `properties`. Covered: GET /api/settings/safety-limits → min_glucose_mgdl, max_glucose_mgdl; GET /api/settings/alert-thresholds → urgent_low, low_warning, high_warning, urgent_high; POST /api/auth/mobile/login → access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, user. assertArrayItemFieldsPresent additionally descends properties[arrayProperty].items for GET /api/integrations/nightscout/{connection_id}/data → pump_events[units, event_type] and glucose_readings[value]. Note the spec path is written with the SPEC's snake_case `{connection_id}`, not Retrofit's `{connectionId}` — this lookup is unnormalized.
edge_cases: responseSchema()/resolveRef() only follow a TOP-LEVEL $ref; a $ref nested under allOf/oneOf/anyOf would throw JSONException rather than resolve.
Only field NAMES are checked — a type change on these fields is not caught by this test.
The path literal is hardcoded snake_case; a spec path-param rename breaks the test with a JSONException, not a clean assertion failure.

capabilities.name: Nightscout pump_events.units — the nullable-consumed exception
capabilities.behavior: NightscoutPumpEventDto declares `val units: Float? = null`. The Room mapper DROPS any pump event whose `units` is null, so a silent backend rename of `units` would delete all Nightscout bolus/basal rows and understate IOB — with no parse error. Because it is nullable, the round-trip tests cannot catch it; it is covered ONLY by assertArrayItemFieldsPresent on the pinned spec. ADR 0003 states the standing rule explicitly: when adding a nullable consumed field whose absence would silently degrade a safety surface, add it to the field-presence coupling rather than relying on the round-trip. The pinned spec today declares pump_events items {duration_minutes, event_timestamp, event_type, is_automated, meal_event_id, metadata_json, ns_id, source, units} and glucose_readings items {ns_id, reading_timestamp, source, trend, trend_rate, value}.
edge_cases: Silent IOB understatement is the failure mode — no exception, no user-visible error.
NightscoutGlucoseReadingDto.value is a non-null Int, so its removal DOES throw.

capabilities.name: What the smoke test does NOT prove (documented blind spots)
capabilities.behavior: Stated in contract/README.md and ADR 0003. A pass proves only: the exercised responses round-trip, the enumerated safety-critical field names still exist, and endpoint/method presence. It does NOT prove every schema change is additive, and it is not a DTO↔spec structural diff. Blind spots: (a) removal of a nullable/defaulted consumed field deserializes to null silently — only non-null undefaulted fields (glucose bounds, auth tokens) fail loudly, and the README says keep it that way; (b) type changes on non-exercised surfaces; (c) path-parameter renames (normalized away); (d) request-body schema drift (only responses are checked); (e) enum-member and nullability changes; (f) anything about a runtime backend — the guard fires only when the pin is refreshed.
edge_cases: README instructs: "Review schema changes to surfaces the smoke test does not exercise before relying on the pass."

capabilities.name: ADR 0001 Decision 1 — endpoint versioning left as-is
capabilities.behavior: Accepted. The backend's `/api/*` versioning will NOT be normalized. Only /api/v1/devices, /api/v1/alerts (incl. alert_stream), /api/v1/api-keys, /api/v1/glucose/stream are version-prefixed; the rest (/api/auth/…, /api/settings/…, /api/ai/…, /api/food-records, most /api/integrations/…) are unversioned. The split is historical, not designed. Stated reasons: normalization is a runtime backend change out of scope for guard-only work, and it would break every unversioned path the already-shipped app calls unless done with parallel routing (large, risky). The contract pin + drift gate already makes the whole surface explicit and CI-enforced, which was the property actually needed. Standing rule for the future: if a breaking change to an unversioned path is unavoidable, introduce a /v2 sibling and keep the old path until the shipped fleet ages out — never mutate an unversioned path in place.
edge_cases: Revisit trigger: an unavoidable breaking change to an unversioned path.

capabilities.name: ADR 0001 Decision 2 — app-compatibility signal (designed, NOT implemented)
capabilities.behavior: Deliberately deferred: "design now, implement later"; no runtime path ships. Design: backend exposes x-contract-version over a stable runtime channel — an `X-Contract-Version` response header on /health or a field in the /health body (neither exists today). The app pins the minimum contract version it requires (contract/CONTRACT_VERSION, the version it was built and tested against) and compares on first contact. Ordering: CONTRACT_VERSION is a monotonically increasing integer starting at 1, not semver and not opaque; comparison is numeric. A value that fails to parse as an integer, or a signal the app cannot read, is treated as ABSENT — the older/unknown-backend branch — never silently as compatible. Reason for deferral: this work is guard-only and adds no runtime path.
edge_cases: Unparseable version must NOT be treated as compatible — fail toward the warning branch.
No /health header or body field exists in the pinned spec today.

capabilities.name: Scoped fail-open-with-warning state machine (designed)
capabilities.behavior: Three states on first contact with a backend: (1) signal present AND app-required ≤ backend version → proceed normally. (2) signal present AND backend older than the app requires, OR (3) signal absent/unparseable → proceed on READ/MONITORING paths with a one-time, dismissible warning that the backend is older/unknown and some features may not work; individual failing calls are handled per-call, not by blocking the app. The app MUST NOT hard-refuse for an unknown backend — that would brick a legitimate self-hoster on upgrade. Scope limit (load-bearing): fail-open applies to reading/displaying only because the app is monitoring-only and issues no therapeutic/device-control commands (no bolus, no pump writes; the AI never issues device commands — a project-wide invariant). Any future safety-critical WRITE surface must be REFUSED when backend compatibility is unknown, not inherit fail-open. Hard-refuse of the whole app is reserved for a future explicitly-declared hard-incompatibility epoch.
edge_cases: Revisit trigger: adding any therapeutic or safety-critical write surface.
Warning must be one-time and dismissible, not a recurring modal.

capabilities.name: ADR 0002 — backend tolerant reader (server half)
capabilities.behavior: Accepted; records existing backend behavior as THE cross-cadence compatibility mechanism, to be preserved deliberately. Two named mechanisms: (1) legacy-value migration BEFORE validation — apps/api/src/schemas/pump.py `migrate_control_iq_mode`; `control_iq_mode` is a loose `str | None` (not an enum) and the legacy value `standard` is rewritten to `none` pre-validation, so an older app still sending `standard` is accepted rather than 422'd. (2) loose-typed pass-through fields — `raw_events` and `pump_info` on the pump-push schema are intentionally typed `Any`, with an explicit "shape has drifted slightly" note; new optional fields the app doesn't know, or fields the app omits, do not break the exchange. Consequence clause: any future backend change removing tolerant-reader behavior (tightening raw_events/pump_info, dropping a legacy migration) is a cross-cadence BREAKING change — bump the contract version and coordinate with the shipped fleet.
edge_cases: The Android PumpEventDto still carries `control_iq_mode` as a nullable String — matching the loose backend type.

capabilities.name: ADR 0002 — supported compatibility directions (explicit)
capabilities.behavior: The mechanism is DIRECTIONAL and only two directions are established. (1) Older app → newer backend: covered by the backend legacy-value migration and loose-typed pass-through fields. (2) Newer backend → older app: covered by Moshi ignoring unknown fields on the client. NOT established: newer app → older backend — an app calling a backend that predates a field/endpoint it now expects. That third case is handled defensively, not proven-compatible, via the scoped fail-open-with-warning and per-call error handling of ADR 0001 plus the app's on-device defaults where a setting can't be fetched. Explicit instruction: do not treat the tolerant reader as a blanket cross-cadence guarantee; where a specific operation must be compatibility-gated, gate it per ADR 0001 rather than assuming tolerance.
edge_cases: A Swift port shipping ahead of the backend lands in the unproven third direction by default.

capabilities.name: ADR 0003 Decision 1 — smoke test over full DTO↔spec diff
capabilities.behavior: Accepted, with the rejected alternative recorded. A full automated DTO-to-OpenAPI structural diff (walk every DTO field, resolve its $ref, compare types/nullability/enum members) was deliberately NOT built. Stated reasons: it needs a Kotlin-reflection + JSON-Schema resolver modelling Moshi @Json(name=…) renames, defaulted/nullable semantics, Instant adapters, and polymorphism — substantial test infrastructure to maintain; and the genuine risk is narrow (a field the app READS disappearing or changing type, or an endpoint the app CALLS being dropped). The smoke test delivers the needed compatibility signal at a fraction of the cost. Pin-update procedure recorded here too: refresh openapi.json byte-for-byte, update CONTRACT_VERSION to match, reconcile affected fixtures; if endpoint-presence or a golden round-trip then fails, the change is incompatible and needs a coordinated app change.
edge_cases: No revisit trigger is stated for Decision 1; the blind-spot rule (add nullable consumed fields to field-presence coupling) is the ongoing obligation.

capabilities.name: ADR 0003 Decision 2 — safety constants: guard now, consolidate later
capabilities.behavior: The three cross-repo safety constants are guarded by SafetyConstantDriftGuardTest via direct constant reads, behavioral boundary checks, and a comment-stripped source scan of every shipped duplication site. The 20..500 mg/dL bound is genuinely scattered with NO single owner (the ADR is explicit that 18.0156 is unrelated — it is only the mmol/L display-conversion factor, not a bound), so the guard asserts EVERY current duplication site rather than one constant. Consolidating the bound into a single shared object with all call sites referencing it is recorded as the right end state and an explicit FOLLOW-UP; it is deliberately not bundled because it edits safety validators (require/init blocks in BgmReading, PluginEvent, EnrichedBolusEvent, CgmReading, SafetyLimits) and would enlarge the blast radius of a guard-only change. Acknowledged cost: adding a duplication site requires updating the guard enumeration AND safety-constants.md in the same PR.
edge_cases: A Swift port should consolidate up front rather than reproduce 19 scattered sites.

capabilities.name: Safety constant #1 — mmol↔mg/dL factor 18.0156
capabilities.behavior: Canonical value 18.0156 (Double). Backend owner: apps/api/src/core/units.py MGDL_PER_MMOL; web has a matching MGDL_PER_MMOL. Android sites: GlucoseFormat.MGDL_PER_MMOL (phone choke-point) and GlucoseDisplayUtils.MGDL_PER_MMOL (wear mirror; wear cannot depend on :app). Both KDocs forbid introducing a second value (explicitly naming 18.02 and 18.0182 as wrong). Canonical storage is mg/dL everywhere; mmol/L is display/input ONLY; alert and SSE numerics stay mg/dL. Conversion rule: divide ONCE from the most precise mg/dL source and round LAST to one decimal, so anchors land conventionally: 70→3.9, 180→10.0, 120→6.7, 100→5.6. All formatting uses Locale.US so the separator is always a dot (cross-surface consistency and release-log-scrubber matching).
edge_cases: Rounding early (e.g. converting an already-rounded value) breaks the 70→3.9 / 180→10.0 anchors.
Locale-sensitive formatting would emit a comma separator and break scrubbing.

capabilities.name: GlucoseFormat API surface (phone conversion choke-point)
capabilities.behavior: Pure-Kotlin object, no Android deps, so the watch can mirror it. label(): "mg/dL"/"mmol/L". spokenUnit(): "milligrams per deciliter"/"millimoles per liter". private mgdlToMmol(Double) = value / 18.0156 (mirrors backend mgdl_to_mmol). convertValue(mgDl: Int, unit): Double — verbatim for MGDL, unrounded divide for MMOL. convertSpread(mgDl: Double): Double — offset-free divide, deliberately DISTINCT from convertValue because a spread (std-dev or difference) has no zero anchor and keeps a decimal in mg/dL where a value shows as an integer; reusing convertValue for a spread is called out as a bug. format(): mg/dL integer via toString, mmol "%.1f". formatWithLabel() joins with a space. formatMean(Float): mg/dL "%.0f" (byte-identical to the legacy string), mmol "%.1f". formatSpread(Float): one decimal in BOTH units, mmol via convertSpread.
edge_cases: convertValue vs convertSpread confusion is an explicitly named bug class.
mg/dL mean uses %.0f (half-up-ish Java formatting), not truncation.

capabilities.name: Wear GlucoseDisplayUtils (mirror + on-watch clamps)
capabilities.behavior: object in :wear-device. MGDL_PER_MMOL = 18.0156. isValidGlucose(mgDl) = mgDl in 20..500. sanitizeThresholds(rawLow, rawHigh, rawUrgentLow, rawUrgentHigh): low = rawLow.coerceIn(40, 200); high = rawHigh.coerceIn(maxOf(low+1, 100), 400); urgentLow = rawUrgentLow.coerceIn(20, low); urgentHigh = rawUrgentHigh.coerceIn(high, 500). bgColor: red 0xFFEF4444 when mgDl ≤ urgentLow or ≥ urgentHigh; yellow 0xFFEAB308 when ≤ low or ≥ high; else green 0xFF22C55E. alertColor: "urgent_low"/"urgent_high" red, "low"/"high" yellow, else Color.WHITE. formatGlucose/formatWithLabel mirror the phone (Locale.US, %.1f mmol). trendSymbol maps DOUBLE_UP ⇈ / SINGLE_UP ↑ / FORTY_FIVE_UP ↗ / FLAT → / FORTY_FIVE_DOWN ↘ / SINGLE_DOWN ↓ / DOUBLE_DOWN ⇊ / else "?". formatAge: < −STATUS_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS → "unknown time"; <0 → "just now"; <1 min → "just now"; <60 min → "Nm ago"; else "Xh Ym ago".
edge_cases: KDoc warns: never feed formatGlucose output back into isValidGlucose, bgColor, sanitizeThresholds, or plotting geometry — those stay mg/dL.
The two coerceIn clamps (20, low) and (high, 500) are individually enumerated scan sites.

capabilities.name: Safety constant #2 — the 20..500 mg/dL glucose-validity bound
capabilities.behavior: Canonical: 20..500 mg/dL inclusive. Backend owner is not a single symbol but the platform invariant from PR #729, enforced by the CodeRabbit Medical-Safety gate in .coderabbit.yaml; the backend rejects outside this range at every ingestion mapper and on GlucoseReading (ge=20). Android has NO single owner today — the closest is SafetyLimits (DEFAULT_MIN_GLUCOSE / DEFAULT_MAX_GLUCOSE and the ABSOLUTE_* aliases), from which SafetyLimitsStore defaults derive. The bound appears as: importable public consts (SafetyLimits, CgmReading), private consts (DashboardComputations, HomeViewModel), inline `20..500` range literals in require/validation blocks, a SQL `BETWEEN 20 AND 500`, off-by-one forms `20..499`/`21..500`, and two wear coerceIn clamps. Any legitimate change must land in BOTH repos in the same coordinated release, with safety-constants.md and the guard enumeration updated in the same PR.
edge_cases: Desync here means glucose is mis-validated — readings silently accepted or dropped.
Bound is inclusive on both ends; 20 and 500 are valid.

capabilities.name: SafetyLimits value object (bounds, defaults, safeOf clamping)
capabilities.behavior: data class SafetyLimits(minGlucoseMgDl=DEFAULT_MIN_GLUCOSE, maxGlucoseMgDl=DEFAULT_MAX_GLUCOSE, maxBasalRateMilliunits=DEFAULT_MAX_BASAL_MILLIUNITS, maxBolusDoseMilliunits=DEFAULT_MAX_BOLUS_MILLIUNITS). Constants: DEFAULT_MIN_GLUCOSE=20, DEFAULT_MAX_GLUCOSE=500, DEFAULT_MAX_BASAL_MILLIUNITS=15_000 (15 U/hr, Tandem hardware max), DEFAULT_MAX_BOLUS_MILLIUNITS=25_000 (25 U single dose); ABSOLUTE_MIN_GLUCOSE/ABSOLUTE_MAX_GLUCOSE/ABSOLUTE_MAX_BASAL_MILLIUNITS/ABSOLUTE_MAX_BOLUS_MILLIUNITS alias the DEFAULT_* values — no backend configuration may widen them. init requires: min ≥ 20; max ≤ 500; min < max; basal in 1..15000; bolus in 1..25000 — each with a specific message. safeOf(...) is the lenient factory for untrusted/backend input: clampedMin = min.coerceIn(20, 499); clampedMax = max.coerceIn(clampedMin+1, 500); basal.coerceIn(1, 15000); bolus.coerceIn(1, 25000) — clamps instead of throwing.
edge_cases: Constructor is strict (throws) for programmatic callers; safeOf is lenient for external data — a crash was judged worse than clamped values there.
ABSOLUTE_* are aliases, so widening a DEFAULT silently widens the absolute ceiling too.

capabilities.name: Domain validators enforcing 20..500 (behavioral boundary)
capabilities.behavior: Four constructors throw IllegalArgumentException outside the bound; the guard exercises each at min, max, min−1, max+1. BgmReading(glucoseMgDl, timestamp, meterName?) — `require(glucoseMgDl in 20..500) { "glucoseMgDl must be in 20..500, was $glucoseMgDl" }`. CgmReading(glucoseMgDl, trendArrow: CgmTrend, timestamp) — `require(glucoseMgDl in MIN_MG_DL..MAX_MG_DL)` with MIN_MG_DL=20, MAX_MG_DL=500. PluginEvent.CalibrationRequested(pluginId, bgValueMgDl, timestamp) — `require(bgValueMgDl in 20..500)`. EnrichedBolusEvent — `bgAtEvent?.let { require(it in 20..500) { "bgAtEvent must be 20-500 mg/dL" } }`, so null bgAtEvent is allowed; it additionally requires units, correctionUnits, and mealUnits each in 0f..BolusEvent.MAX_BOLUS_UNITS. CgmTrend enum: DOUBLE_UP, SINGLE_UP, FORTY_FIVE_UP, FLAT, FORTY_FIVE_DOWN, SINGLE_DOWN, DOUBLE_DOWN, UNKNOWN.
edge_cases: Construction-time throwing means an out-of-range reading crashes the caller unless caught — parsers are expected to filter first.
EnrichedBolusEvent's message uses a hyphen ("20-500"), so it contributes only ONE `20..500` token to the scan.

capabilities.name: Safety constant #3 — Tandem epoch offset 1199145600
capabilities.behavior: Canonical 1_199_145_600 seconds = Unix time of 2008-01-01T00:00:00Z. Backend owner: apps/api/src/core/tandem_regions.py TANDEM_EPOCH_OFFSET_SECONDS. Android site: `private const val TANDEM_EPOCH_OFFSET = 1199145600L` in StatusResponseParser (internal object; no importable accessor, hence the source scan). pumpTimeToInstant(pumpTimeSec): rawEpochSec = pumpTimeSec + 1199145600; localDateTime = LocalDateTime.ofEpochSecond(rawEpochSec, 0, ZoneOffset.UTC); return localDateTime.atZone(ZoneId.systemDefault()).toInstant(). The UTC offset is intentional: the pump counts seconds since LOCAL midnight 2008-01-01 and the constant is UTC-based, so interpreting at UTC extracts the correct wall-clock LocalDateTime fields, which are then re-anchored to the device zone. All parsers in this object return null on malformed cargo rather than throwing.
edge_cases: Drift here shifts every Tandem event timestamp — mis-ordering insulin history and IOB.
The double-conversion (UTC decode then systemDefault re-anchor) is load-bearing; a naive Instant.ofEpochSecond would be wrong by the device's UTC offset.

capabilities.name: Drift guard scan matching algorithm (countOccurrences + stripComments)
capabilities.behavior: countOccurrences(text, token) = Regex("(?<![0-9])" + Regex.escape(token) + "(?![0-9eE._])").findAll(text).count(). The trailing lookahead rejects a following digit, `.`, `_`, `e`, or `E`, so widening/precision drift cannot slip through as a prefix match: 20..500→20..5000, 18.0156→18.01565, 18.0156→18.0156e1 all stop matching. The leading lookbehind rejects only a preceding digit (so 120..500 doesn't match) and deliberately NOT `.` or `_`, so a method-call token like `.coerceIn(20, low)` still matches. A trailing `L` is not excluded, so `1199145600L` still matches its token. stripComments removes /* … */ (DOT_MATCHES_ALL, so KDoc too) then truncates each line at the first `//`. Rationale: comment edits must not trip the guard, and a comment mention must not mask a code-level change.
edge_cases: stripComments is naive: a `//` inside a string literal or a URL would truncate that line, and a `/*` inside a string would eat code.
Because widening is caught only by the token boundary, replacing 500 with 600 changes the count to 0 and fails — the intended behavior.

capabilities.name: Backend-response validation sites (reject-and-ignore rules)
capabilities.behavior: AuthRepository applies the bound to three fetched settings and IGNORES the whole response on violation (logs Timber.w, returns; does not throw, does not partially apply). Target glucose range: ul/lo/hi/uh = roundToInt of urgentLow/lowTarget/highTarget/urgentHigh; reject unless all in 20..500 AND ul<lo<hi<uh. Alert thresholds: ul/lw/hw/uh roundToInt; reject unless all in 20..500 AND server ordering urgentLow<lowWarning<highWarning<urgentHigh. Rejecting the response leaves the previously stored thresholds in effect — the alert floor keeps firing on stale values.

capabilities.name: SettingsViewModel threshold input/display conversion
capabilities.behavior: parseThresholdMgDl(raw, unit): trim, replace ',' with '.', toDoubleOrNull (null → not-a-number error), reject non-finite; MGDL → roundToInt(); MMOL → (value * 18.0156).roundToInt() — i.e. input is converted to canonical mg/dL BEFORE bounds checking. Validation then errors with "Enter a number for all four thresholds." when any parse fails; "Thresholds must be between <bounds>." when any of ul/lw/hw/uh is !in 20..500; "Thresholds must increase: urgent low ≤ low < high ≤ urgent high." when ordering fails. thresholdBoundsLabel(unit): MGDL → "20 and 500 mg/dL"; MMOL → min = ceil((20 − 0.5) × 10 / 18.0156)/10 and max = floor((500 + 0.499) × 10 / 18.0156)/10, i.e. "1.1 and 27.7 mmol/L". The documented reason: the naive conversion of 500 is 27.8, which rounds back to 501 mg/dL and would be rejected by the very message quoting it — so the quoted bounds are the outermost 0.1-step values whose conversion is accepted.
edge_cases: Comma decimal separators are accepted on input but output always uses a dot (Locale.US).
A Swift port that quotes naive mmol bounds will produce a self-rejecting error message.

AI_TOOLS = claude|anthropic|copilot|chatgpt|openai|cursor|windsurf|codeium|codewhisperer|amazon\.q|gemini|gemini\.code\.assist|jetbrains\.ai|tabnine|sourcegraph|cody|devin|aider|codex. capabilities.name: CodeRabbit Medical-Safety gate (the 20-500 bound's cross-repo enforcer)
capabilities.behavior: .coderabbit.yaml declares custom_checks with mode "error". "Medical Safety Review": for PRs touching glucose values, insulin/pump telemetry, or unit conversions — glucose is STORED and COMPARED in canonical mg/dL; every persisted field, bound, threshold/alert comparison, dedup key, and safety check must stay mg/dL and be bounds-checked to 20-500. mmol/L is display/input only; the single allowed factor is 18.0156. Hard-FAIL if code stores/compares a mmol value as mg/dL (e.g. persisting 3.9 instead of ~70 — "this silently suppresses low alerts"), converts the wrong direction, permits a stored mg/dL outside 20-500 after conversion, or uses any factor other than 18.0156. Do NOT flag a user-facing mmol display literal (3.9, 10.0, 22.2) or an mmol input converted before storage. Also verifies no auto-bolus / therapeutic device-command code exists (monitoring-only, read-only) and that AI suggestions carry safety disclaimers. Sibling checks: "No Hardcoded Secrets" and "BLE Protocol Safety" (GATT timeouts + serialization, connection-state transitions, Little-Endian for Tandem, no raw pump data/serials/auth material at INFO level).
edge_cases: This gate is cited by safety-constants.md as the backend-side owner of the 20-500 invariant (PR #729) — there is no single backend constant to import.

safety_critical: Glucose validity bound 20..500 mg/dL (inclusive) is duplicated across 19 enumerated Android code sites with NO single owner. A desync in any one silently accepts or drops readings. The drift guard is a count-equality source scan, not a real single-source-of-truth — a Swift port must consolidate to one constant.

mmol↔mg/dL factor 18.0156 exists in two Android copies (GlucoseFormat, wear GlucoseDisplayUtils) and must equal the backend's core/units.py MGDL_PER_MMOL. Using 18.02 or 18.0182 is explicitly forbidden. Convert ONCE from the most precise mg/dL source and round LAST to one decimal (70→3.9, 180→10.0, 120→6.7, 100→5.6).

Canonical storage/comparison unit is mg/dL everywhere; mmol/L is display and input only. Alert and SSE numerics stay mg/dL. Persisting a mmol value as mg/dL (3.9 instead of ~70) silently suppresses low alerts — CodeRabbit hard-fails this.

Alert thresholds fetched from /api/settings/alert-thresholds are what the ON-DEVICE alert floor fires from; the app must alarm at exactly the server's levels. If validation rejects a response, the previously stored thresholds keep firing (stale-threshold risk).

Nightscout pump_events[].units is nullable-consumed: a null DROPS the event, so a silent backend rename deletes all NS bolus/basal and UNDERSTATES IOB with no error. Only the pinned-spec field-presence check catches it.

Tandem epoch offset 1199145600 s (2008-01-01 UTC) with the deliberate UTC-decode-then-systemDefault-reanchor conversion. Drift or a naive Instant.ofEpochSecond shifts every pump event timestamp and mis-orders insulin history/IOB.

SafetyLimits absolute bounds: glucose 20..500, max basal 15_000 mU/hr, max bolus 25_000 mU. ABSOLUTE_* alias DEFAULT_*, so widening a default widens the absolute ceiling. safeOf() CLAMPS untrusted backend input rather than throwing (min→20..499, max→(min+1)..500).

App is monitoring-only: no therapeutic or device-control commands, no bolus, no pump writes; the AI never issues device commands (project-wide invariant). Fail-open-with-warning for an unknown backend applies ONLY to read/monitoring paths; any future safety-critical write must be refused when compatibility is unknown.

AlertThresholdStore.requireSafeThresholds THROWS on out-of-range or mis-ordered thresholds while AuthRepository silently ignores the response — two different failure modes for the same data. Ordering strictness also differs (strict < in AuthRepository's range check vs ≤/</≤ in AlertThresholdStore).

Wear-side clamps are a second, independent bound expression: sanitizeThresholds low∈40..200, high∈max(low+1,100)..400, urgentLow∈20..low, urgentHigh∈high..500, plus isValidGlucose 20..500. Watch and phone must not disagree on the same mg/dL value.

Model Instant as Date with a custom decoding strategy that accepts ISO-8601 both with and without fractional seconds (ISO8601DateFormatter needs .withFractionalSeconds explicitly, unlike Instant.parse) and throws DecodingError.dataCorrupted on failure. needs_redesign.why: Half of this ports free and half breaks silently. Swift's synthesised Codable ignores unknown keys (matching Moshi) and decodes a missing key for an Optional-typed property to nil. But a NON-optional property with a Swift default value does NOT tolerate a missing key — the synthesised decoder throws .keyNotFound and ignores the default. Kotlin constructor defaults are exactly what makes absent-optional tolerated today, so a mechanical port turns fields like NightscoutConnectionDto.isActive = true and NightscoutPumpEventDto.isAutomated = false from tolerant into hard failures.
options: Make every defaulted field Optional and apply the default at the mapping layer — changes the domain type shape.
Hand-write init(from:) using decodeIfPresent(...) ?? default for each defaulted field — explicit, verbose, auditable.
A @Defaulted property wrapper (or a macro) that supplies decodeIfPresent semantics with a declared default — concise but adds machinery.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Property wrapper / macro for the common case, hand-written init(from:) for the safety-critical models. Whichever is chosen, add a test that enumerates every model field the Android side declares with a Kotlin default and asserts that omitting that key decodes successfully — otherwise this regression is invisible until an older backend is hit. Keep the existing two tolerance tests (unknown extra fields incl. unknown nested objects; glucose_unit_source absent → nil) as-is.

Swift has no runtime metadata for method attributes and Mirror cannot see them, so the list cannot be derived from the client at test time. The guard must instead couple to something the client is structurally forced to use.

needs_redesign.why: The deferral rationale was "this work is guard-only and adds no runtime path." That rationale does not survive the iOS distribution model. Under fork-and-build, every user compiles from an arbitrary commit at an arbitrary time and points it at their own self-hosted backend of arbitrary age, so app/backend version skew becomes the normal case rather than an edge case. On Android the shipped fleet moves as one; on iOS it does not.
options: Port the ADR as a design and stay deferred, matching Android exactly.

Implement only the READ side now: parse an X-Contract-Version response header on /health (or a body field), compare numerically against the built-in CONTRACT_VERSION, treat missing/unparseable as absent — inert until the backend ships the signal, zero cost if it never does.
Implement read side plus a version handshake gate on first contact with a new backend URL.

It is a few dozen lines, it is dead code until the backend emits the signal, and it means a self-hoster who upgrades the app ahead of the backend gets a real warning instead of scattered per-call failures. Keep ADR 0001's ordering rules verbatim: monotonically increasing integer starting at 1, numeric comparison, never semver, unparseable treated as absent and routed to the older/unknown branch — never silently as compatible.

needs_redesign.capability: ADR 0002 — supported compatibility directions
needs_redesign.why: ADR 0002 establishes only two proven directions (older app → newer backend via backend legacy-value migration and loose pass-through fields; newer backend → older app via client unknown-field tolerance). The third — newer app → older backend — is explicitly NOT established and is handled defensively. A source-distributed iOS app built from HEAD by each user lands in that unproven third direction by default, on day one, for every user whose backend lags their last build.
options: Accept the defensive posture unchanged and rely on per-call error handling plus on-device defaults.
Document and enforce a minimum backend contract version in the fork-and-build README and in the app's backend-setup flow.
Implement the ADR 0001 compat signal so the unproven direction is at least detected.
needs_redesign.recommendation: All three, in that order of cheapness: keep per-call handling and on-device defaults as the floor; state the minimum backend version the build was validated against in the release notes and on the in-app About/diagnostics screen; implement the read-side compat signal. Preserve the explicit instruction not to treat the tolerant reader as a blanket cross-cadence guarantee — gate specific operations per ADR 0001 rather than assuming tolerance.

needs_redesign.capability: ADR 0003 Decision 1 — smoke test chosen over a full DTO↔spec structural diff
needs_redesign.why: The decision may well land the same way, but its stated rationale no longer holds and must be re-taken. The alternative was rejected because it would require building a Kotlin-reflection + JSON-Schema resolver modelling @Json renames, defaulted/nullable semantics and Instant adapters. In Swift that infrastructure exists off the shelf: swift-openapi-generator consumes the pin at build time and supports a `filter:` restricted to specific operations, so structural drift on the covered surface becomes a compile error rather than a test assertion.
options: Keep the hand-written models + smoke test exactly as on Android — cheapest, preserves full hand control over tolerant-reader semantics.
Generate a filtered client from the pin for the 34 operations and map generated types into domain models — turns endpoint presence and response-shape drift into build failures.
Full generation from all 164 paths / 274 schemas — large generated surface, slow builds, no benefit on unused endpoints.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Keep the smoke test as the shipped posture (option 1), and record option 2 as evaluated-and-declined with a reason, so the ADR stays honest. The decisive argument for hand-written models is the nullable-consumed exception: generated types make every spec-required field required and every optional field optional, which removes the ability to deliberately declare a field non-optional so it fails loudly (auth tokens, glucose bounds) while another stays optional-but-field-presence-checked (pump_events.units). That hand-tuned asymmetry IS the safety design. Re-evaluate if the covered surface grows well past 34 operations.

needs_redesign.why: The follow-up should become the design. Android deferred consolidation because it edits safety validators and would enlarge a guard-only change's blast radius, and because :wear-device cannot depend on :app so the wear copy is structurally forced. Neither constraint exists on iOS: a plain Swift SPM target with no platform dependencies is importable by the iOS app, the watchOS app, widget and complication extensions, and every compile-time-linked pump driver module. There is nothing to force a second copy.
options: Reproduce the 19 scattered sites and port the count-equality scan guard for parity.
Consolidate up front into one shared target and replace the enumeration scan with direct constant reads plus an inverse forbidden-literal scan.
Consolidate the named constants but leave inline literals in validators.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Consolidate up front (option 2). One `GlucoseSafety` enum (mgdlPerMmol, validRange 20...500, and the derived clamp sub-ranges) in a shared target; every validator, view model, store, chart clamp and persistence predicate references it. This is the single largest safety win available in this subsystem: it converts a 19-site count-equality guard into a real single source of truth, and it retires the acknowledged cost that adding a duplication site requires updating both the guard enumeration and safety-constants.md in the same PR.

(1) Rounding mode: Java's String.format("%.0f") rounds HALF_UP, so formatMean(72.5) → "73"; C/Swift printf uses the IEEE round-half-to-even mode, so String(format:"%.0f", 72.5) → "72". The mg/dL mean string is explicitly documented as byte-identical to a legacy string, so this is a visible parity break. (2) Locale: String(format:) with no locale is non-localised and safe, but NumberFormatter and the modern .formatted() FormatStyle localise by default and would emit a comma separator, breaking cross-surface consistency and release-log scrubbing.

Round explicitly with .rounded(.toNearestOrAwayFromZero) before formatting, then format the already-rounded value.
Route all numeric formatting through a NumberFormatter pinned to Locale(identifier:"en_US_POSIX") with roundingMode = .halfUp.

Add unit tests at exact tie values (72.5, 137.5) to lock the behaviour. Preserve the convertValue/convertSpread distinction exactly — a spread has no zero anchor, keeps a decimal in mg/dL where a value shows as an integer, and reusing convertValue for a spread remains a named bug class. Add a lint rule banning .formatted() and unpinned NumberFormatter on any glucose value.

ios_requirements: The repository must vendor a byte-for-byte copy of the backend's OpenAPI contract at Contract/openapi.json alongside a Contract/CONTRACT_VERSION file, and a maintainer must be able to refresh both in a single PR by copying the whole spec and setting the version from info.x-contract-version — never by hand-editing the spec.
A maintainer must be able to run the full contract guard suite locally on a Mac in seconds without an iOS Simulator, an App Store Connect account, or a network connection.

CI must fail any PR in which the vendored CONTRACT_VERSION does not equal info.x-contract-version inside the pinned spec, with a message telling the developer to refresh the pin and its version together.

CI must fail any PR in which an endpoint or HTTP method the app calls is absent from the pinned spec, naming Contract/openapi.json in the failure, and the app's networking layer must expose its complete endpoint list to the test rather than hiding it behind hand-written URL construction.

CI must fail any PR in which the pinned spec stops declaring a field the app consumes on a safety-critical response: safety-limits min/max glucose, alert-thresholds urgent_low/low_warning/high_warning/urgent_high, login access_token/refresh_token/expires_in/user, and the Nightscout data array items pump_events[units, event_type] and glucose_readings[value].

The project must maintain a written standing rule, enforced in review, that any newly consumed optional field whose absence would silently degrade a safety surface is added to the pinned-spec field-presence check rather than left to round-trip tests.
The app must decode responses through exactly one shared decoder configuration, and the contract tests must exercise that same object, so the test cannot silently diverge from what ships.

The app must tolerate a newer backend adding unknown fields, including unknown nested objects, and must tolerate an older backend omitting any field the app treats as optional or defaulted — including fields with non-nil defaults, which require explicit handling in Swift.

The app must fail loudly and refuse to use a response when a field it treats as required is renamed, removed, or sent with the wrong scalar type, and must never coerce a JSON string into a numeric field.
The app must never model a backend-supplied enumerated value as a strict enum; any unrecognised member must decode to a well-defined unknown case rather than failing the whole response.

The app must read a backend contract-version signal where one is offered, compare it numerically against the version the build was validated against, and treat a missing or unparseable signal as an older/unknown backend — never as compatible.

On first contact with a backend that is older or of unknown version, the app must continue to work on all read and monitoring paths and show a single dismissible warning that some features may not work; it must never refuse to run, and it must never show that warning at all when no backend is configured (local mode).

The app must show the user which upstream commit it was built from, which contract version it was validated against, and which backend it is paired with, on a screen reachable without a backend connection.

There must be exactly one definition in the codebase of the 20-500 mg/dL glucose validity bound and exactly one definition of the 18.0156 mmol conversion factor, shared unchanged by the iPhone app, the Apple Watch app, every widget and complication extension, and every compile-time-linked pump driver.
CI must fail any PR that introduces a hardcoded glucose bound or conversion factor outside those canonical definitions.

Glucose must be stored and compared in mg/dL on every surface; mmol/L must exist only as display and input; converting must divide once from the most precise mg/dL source and round last so that 70 shows as 3.9, 100 as 5.6, 120 as 6.7 and 180 as 10.0 on both phone and watch.

Every numeric glucose string the app produces must use a dot decimal separator and half-up rounding regardless of the device's locale, and must be byte-identical between phone and watch for the same input.

Constructing a domain reading with an out-of-range glucose value must fail in a way the caller can handle; no code path that consumes Bluetooth, backend, or persisted data may terminate the process on invalid input.

The app must reject a backend settings response atomically when any threshold or safety limit is out of range or mis-ordered, retain the last known-good values, and show the user when the values in force were last successfully synced.

A user must be able to enter thresholds in either unit using their own keyboard's decimal separator, and any out-of-range error message must quote bounds that would themselves be accepted if re-entered.

A maintainer must be able to validate every part of this subsystem in the iOS and watchOS Simulators, with no physical iPhone, Apple Watch, or pump — which requires a simulated data source that links against the same shared safety constants as every real driver.

Every shipped source file must carry the project's SPDX header, every file containing ported third-party code must carry that upstream's identifier and copyright instead, and CI must fail a PR that violates either rule — including the EC-JPAKE implementation, which must carry Apache-2.0 attribution in the file itself and not only in a documentation page.

CI must block any PR whose commits, code comments, or description carry AI-tool attribution, using the same severity model, bot allowlist, and auto-close behaviour as the Android repository, extended to Swift source files.

The upstream repository must build, test, lint, and security-scan the app without any Apple signing material, and the fork-and-build release workflow must run every safety and contract guard as a hard prerequisite of producing an installable artifact.

risks.risk: Swift's synthesised Codable throws on a missing key for a non-optional property even when it has a default value. A mechanical port of the Kotlin DTOs converts every defaulted-but-non-null field from tolerant into a hard failure, breaking the newer-backend/older-app compatibility direction ADR 0002 depends on — and it breaks only against an older backend, which upstream CI never exercises.
risks.mitigation: Enumerate every Kotlin DTO field that carries a constructor default and add an explicit omit-this-key decoding test for each. Use a property wrapper or hand-written init(from:) with decodeIfPresent to restore default-on-absent semantics. Add a CI check that flags any non-optional Codable property with a default value.

risks.risk: Under fork-and-build, the newer-app/older-backend direction — the one ADR 0002 explicitly does NOT establish — becomes the normal case for every user whose self-hosted backend lags their last build. Failures surface as scattered per-call errors with no single explanation.
risks.mitigation: Implement the read side of the ADR 0001 compat signal now rather than deferring it, publish the minimum backend contract version each release was validated against, and show it in-app on the About/Diagnostics screen. Keep per-call graceful degradation and on-device defaults as the floor.

risks.risk: Urgent-low alerts may be silent for most users. The critical-alerts entitlement is granted per Apple Developer team on individual request, and under fork-and-build every user signs with their own team. Correct thresholds fetched from the backend do not produce an audible alarm if the phone is on silent.
risks.mitigation: Default to .timeSensitive, upgrade to .critical automatically when the entitlement is present at build time, document the entitlement request and the Time Sensitive permission in the fork-and-build guide, play an in-app alarm when foregrounded, and state the limitation plainly in MEDICAL-DISCLAIMER.md.

risks.risk: A precondition or fatalError on an out-of-range glucose value inside a Core Bluetooth delegate callback during a background state-restoration launch kills the app invisibly; repeated background crashes cause iOS to deprioritise future relaunches, so the app silently stops monitoring. Android's foreground-service crash is at least visible.
risks.mitigation: Ban precondition/fatalError on any value originating from BLE, the backend, or persistence via a SwiftLint custom rule. Use throwing initialisers for domain types and failable initialisers on parser paths so invalid readings are dropped and logged. Add a background-crash counter surfaced on the diagnostics screen.

risks.risk: Java's %.0f rounds half-up while C/Swift printf rounds half-to-even, so a mechanically ported formatMean produces a different string at exact tie values (72.5 → "73" on Android, "72" on iOS). The mg/dL mean string is documented as byte-identical to a legacy string, and glucose values shown differently on two of a user's devices erode trust in the numbers.
risks.mitigation: Round explicitly with .rounded(.toNearestOrAwayFromZero) before formatting rather than relying on the format specifier, and add tie-value unit tests (72.5, 137.5) shared by the phone and watch targets.

risks.risk: The Tandem epoch conversion is not a straight port: Foundation has no LocalDateTime, and a naive Date(timeIntervalSince1970:) is wrong by the device's UTC offset, shifting every pump event timestamp and mis-ordering insulin history and IOB. The error is systematic, plausible-looking, and invisible in a Simulator run in UTC.
risks.mitigation: Implement the UTC-decode-then-device-zone-recompose explicitly with a fixed UTC Calendar and a TimeZone.current snapshot captured at parse time; test in non-UTC zones in both hemispheres and across a DST spring-forward gap; verify against real pump captures on Daniel's t:slim X2.

risks.risk: Swift dependency vulnerability data is materially thinner than Maven's, and OSV-Scanner's Package.resolved support must be verified rather than assumed. The Dependency Scan Gate could be green because nothing is known, not because nothing is wrong.
risks.mitigation: Keep the dependency surface deliberately tiny (the Loop/xDrip4iOS posture), pin every package with .exact(...), commit Package.resolved, run both OSV-Scanner and Dependabot, and record the coverage gap explicitly in docs/dev/security-testing.md with a revisit trigger.

risks.risk: macOS GitHub Actions runners are free for public repositories but bill at a 10x multiplier for private ones. A user who forks privately to keep their backend URL out of public view will burn the free-minute allowance quickly on xcodebuild archives, and may respond by disabling the guard steps in the release workflow.
risks.mitigation: Document that a public fork is safe (GitHub secrets are not exposed in forks) and recommend it. Split CI so the fast host-macOS guard job runs on every push and the expensive Simulator/archive job runs only on release. Make guard steps hard prerequisites of the archive step so disabling them fails the build rather than skipping a check.

risks.risk: The EC-JPAKE attribution gap is still open in the Android repo and gets structurally larger on iOS, where CryptoKit provides no EC-JPAKE at all and every implementation route carries an Apache-2.0 obligation into a GPL-3.0-only source-distributed project.
risks.mitigation: Isolate EC-JPAKE in its own SPM target carrying SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 and the upstream copyright line in the file itself, list it in THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md and in an in-app licences screen, and make the License Header Gate assert its Apache-2.0 line positively rather than merely excluding it. Close the same gap in the Android repo while the policy is fresh.

risks.risk: The lead developer has no iPhone and no Apple Watch, and Core Bluetooth does not exist in the Simulator. Every safety invariant that only manifests on real hardware — background BLE relaunch behaviour, notification audibility, AOD colour legibility, real pump timestamp decoding — is validated by exactly one person on one set of devices.
risks.mitigation: Build the simulated driver as a first-class shipped module linked against the shared safety constants, so bounds, conversion, formatting and threshold logic are fully Simulator-testable. Define an explicit hardware-validation checklist that Daniel runs per release, and record its results against the build's commit SHA.

risks.risk: Consolidating the 20..500 bound into one constant touches every safety validator at once — exactly the blast-radius concern that caused Android to defer it. Doing it up front on iOS is right, but it lands the highest-risk refactor in the codebase before there is a large regression suite behind it.
risks.mitigation: Land the shared constants target and its direct-read tests first, migrate call sites one module at a time with the behavioural boundary tests (min, max, min-1, max+1 on all four domain types) in place before each migration, and turn on the inverse forbidden-literal scan only after the last site has moved.

risks.risk: Contract and drift guards read repository files by path, so they only work when run from inside the repo tree. Running them under an iOS Simulator destination, or relying on the test runner's working directory, produces either a sandbox failure or a silently wrong root.
risks.mitigation: Anchor repo-root resolution on #filePath (baked at compile time) walking up to Package.swift, and run the guards exclusively on a host-macOS SwiftPM test target rather than a Simulator destination.

questions_for_pm: Under fork-and-build, urgent-low alerts will not bypass silent mode or Focus for any user who has not obtained Apple's critical-alerts entitlement for their own developer team — and Apple does not grant that entitlement at scale to individual accounts. Is shipping a glucose monitor whose most safety-relevant alert can be silenced by the ringer switch acceptable for this product, and if so, how should that be disclosed (MEDICAL-DISCLAIMER.md, first-run onboarding, both) and is it acceptable to require each user to attempt the entitlement request as part of setup?
